system.name: OneSidedMW
system.one_liner: an RNIC-offloaded memory management scheme for disaggregated memory that lets compute nodes allocate, free, and access remote memory via one-sided RDMA without memory-node CPU involvement

components.name: CNs
components.role: compute nodes that run tenant applications needing remote memory

components.name: CN runtime (e.g., KVS or swap)
components.role: existing CN-side system (e.g., a disaggregated key-value store or the Linux swap subsystem) that uses OneSidedMW's API

components.name: OneSidedMW API
components.role: provides APIs to allocate, free, and access remote memory without involving the MN's CPU

components.name: RDMA NIC
components.role: issues one-sided RDMA requests from the CN and receives/replies to them at the MN

components.name: MN
components.role: memory node that hosts fine-grained memory chunks managed via memory windows

components.name: Meta Data
components.role: MN-side metadata region holding the WR Chains logic and the Free MW Queue

components.name: WR Chains
components.role: offloaded (de)allocation logic executed by the RNIC itself

components.name: Free MW Queue
components.role: circular-buffer queue of available memory windows, tracked with Head and Tail pointers

components.name: MWTable
components.role: table storing each memory chunk's base address and its memory window's rkey

components.name: MWs
components.role: type-2 memory windows, each pre-allocated and later bound to a memory chunk

components.name: Memory Chunks
components.role: fine-grained, configurable-size units of MN memory that MWs are (un)bound to

flows.what: one-sided RDMA request sent from CN to MN
dequeues (allocates) an MW from the head of the queue
(un)bind the allocated MW to its corresponding memory chunk
returns the MW's metadata (address, rkey) to the requesting CN
each MWTable entry (addr, rkey) corresponds to one MW

content.key_idea: A CN's OneSidedMW API issues a one-sided RDMA request that the MN's RNIC handles alone via offloaded WR Chains: dequeuing a free memory window, binding it to a memory chunk, and returning its address/rkey -- without involving the MN's CPU.
content.reading_order: Left to right, following steps 1-5: CN's OneSidedMW API through the RDMA NICs into the MN's WR Chains, Free MW Queue, MWTable, and MW-Chunk binding, back to the CN.

summary: This figure shows OneSidedMW's architecture and one allocation workflow across the CN/MN (host/device) boundary. On CNs, a CN runtime (e.g., a KVS or the Linux swap subsystem) calls the OneSidedMW API, which issues a one-sided RDMA request over the RDMA NIC (step 1) to the MN's RDMA NIC. There, the offloaded WR Chains logic (step 2) dequeues a free memory window from the circular Free MW Queue, tracked by Head/Tail pointers (step 3), binds that MW to its corresponding Memory Chunk (step 4), and the RDMA NIC returns the MW's address and rkey to the requesting CN (step 5). An MWTable on the MN records each chunk's base address and its MW's rkey, linking table entries to MWs via dashed connectors. The whole allocation and binding runs on the MN's RNIC without involving its CPU.
summary_zh: OneSidedMW架构：CN经RDMA网卡发单边请求(1)；MN的RNIC卸载WR Chains(2)从Free MW Queue取空闲窗口(3)并bind内存块(4)，网卡返回地址rkey给CN(5)，无需MN CPU参与。
